nodes.label: Acronym Casing Rule
nodes.rationale: getHTTPURL() is unreadable without documentation; getHttpUrl() is usable. Acronyms keep only their first letter uppercase inside type and method names; a leading acronym in a field or parameter name is fully lowercase (url), otherwise capitalised first letter (baseUrl).

nodes.label: Methods Named as camelCase Actions
nodes.rationale: Methods read as actions (changeSorting, changeGrouping); prefer the verb 'change' over 'apply'.

nodes.label: verify Prefix for Assertion Methods
nodes.rationale: Starting assertion methods with 'verify' adds readability and makes assertions searchable across the suite.

nodes.label: Test File Naming (_test suffix)
nodes.rationale: Test files use camelCase and must end with _test; the ending is mandatory.

nodes.label: Page Object Pattern
nodes.rationale: Hard-coded locators inside a test are bad practice; every locator lives in a CodeceptJS Page Object.

nodes.label: Stable Locators (data-qa attribute)
nodes.rationale: Ideally every interactive element carries a dedicated data-qa attribute; id, classname and text are the frequent fallbacks, with short XPath preferred.

nodes.label: Locator Preference: locate() > CSS > XPath
nodes.rationale: The locate() builder is first priority, CSS second, XPath is the last resort.

nodes.label: CodeceptJS Built-in Assertions
nodes.rationale: I.seeElement, I.dontSeeElement, I.seeInCurrentUrl may be used directly in a test; non-CodeceptJS assertions only when they cannot live elsewhere.

nodes.label: CodeceptJS Data Provider
nodes.rationale: Same scenario with different data should use a Data Provider to cut code volume and raise maintainability; the reason must be left as a comment.

nodes.label: One Feature per Test File
nodes.rationale: One feature per file lets CodeceptJS split tests across workers so parallel execution is effective, and keeps the suite maintainable; multiple features are allowed only when they share BeforeSteps.

nodes.label: Scenario Title Template
nodes.rationale: Template is {TEST_CASE_ID} Title {annotation}.

nodes.label: Test Case ID from TMT
nodes.rationale: Embedding the original TMT test case ID in the scenario title makes tests searchable.

nodes.label: Test Annotations and Groups
nodes.rationale: Group annotations are appended to the end of the test title, e.g. @pmm-pre-update.

nodes.label: Integrated Alerting (IA)
nodes.rationale: IA alerting UI/API only exists from PMM Server 2.19.0, so the whole suite is gated on that minimum version.

nodes.label: @fb-alerting test tag
nodes.rationale: Single grep tag selects the whole IA suite in the pmm2-ui-tests Jenkins job; the job needs no PMM clients, only the server.

nodes.label: Self-signed SSL webhook receiver
nodes.rationale: Basic auth (alert|alert) plus a self-signed cert exercises IA notification-channel CA validation; fired alerts are asserted by reading testdata/ia/scripts/alert.txt. Tests start the container themselves, so the manual docker-compose steps are only for debugging.

nodes.label: multiple-templates.yml fixture
nodes.rationale: Three sibling templates in one file exercise bulk upload and the per-template listing after a single file add.

nodes.label: range-empty.yaml fixture
nodes.rationale: Negative fixture: the param declares `range:` with no value, so the server must reject or default the missing bounds instead of accepting an unbounded float.

nodes.label: spaceInParam.yml fixture
nodes.rationale: Negative fixture: a parameter name containing a space cannot be a valid Go template identifier, so `[[ .thresh old ]]` must fail validation.

nodes.label: specialCharInParam.yml fixture
nodes.rationale: Negative fixture: `Sp3c@l` puts a non-identifier character in a parameter name to assert the template validator rejects it.

nodes.label: template.txt (non-YAML fixture)
nodes.rationale: Contains only the literal `someText`; used to assert the template upload rejects a file that is neither .yml/.yaml nor parseable as an alert template.

nodes.label: template.yaml fixture
nodes.rationale: Byte-equivalent to template.yml apart from the template name and summary; the pair proves both .yaml and .yml extensions are accepted.

nodes.label: templateForRules.yaml fixture
nodes.rationale: Valid baseline template whose only job is to exist so alert-rule tests have something to build a rule from.

nodes.label: templateWithTiers.yml fixture
nodes.rationale: Identical to inputTemplate.yml plus a `tiers` key, isolating tier gating as the single variable between the two fixtures.

nodes.label: undefinedParam.yml fixture
nodes.rationale: Negative fixture: declares params `from` and `to` but the expression interpolates `[[ .threshold ]]`, which is never defined.

nodes.label: custom_param template
nodes.rationale: Renames the conventional `threshold` parameter to `CustomParam` to prove the UI renders whatever parameter name the template declares.

nodes.label: input_template_yml template (with tiers)
nodes.rationale: Reuses the exact template name of inputTemplate.yml so the tiers variant can be uploaded over the plain one.

nodes.label: threshold param (float %, range 0-100, default 80)
nodes.rationale: Canonical parameter block copied verbatim across nearly every IA fixture, so tests can assert the same unit, type, range and default regardless of which template is uploaded.

nodes.label: MySQL max-connections threshold expression
nodes.rationale: max_over_time(mysql_global_status_threads_connected[5m]) / ignoring(job) mysql_global_variables_max_connections * 100 > [[ .threshold ]]; the shared expression body for the valid IA fixtures.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL max-connections threshold expression
nodes.rationale: sum(pg_stat_activity_count{datname!~"template.*|postgres"}) > bool pg_settings_max_connections * [[ .threshold ]] / 100; excludes template and postgres databases from the connection count.

nodes.label: Severity: warning
nodes.rationale: Every IA fixture template ships severity warning with for: 5m, so severity-filter and rule-edit tests always start from a known non-critical value they can change.

nodes.label: Dual templating: [[ .param ]] vs {{ $labels }}
nodes.rationale: IA substitutes [[ .param ]] at rule-creation time from the template's declared params, while {{ $labels }} / {{ $value }} are left for Alertmanager to expand when the alert fires. Fixtures that break the first form (space, special char, undefined name) must therefore fail on upload, not at alert time.

nodes.label: Mongo Down Nodes States Visual Diff Screenshot
nodes.description: A wide, short capture of a single dark-themed Grafana panel titled 'Node States' with an info tooltip icon. The panel body renders no chart at all - only the centered gray Grafana message 'Data does not have a time field'. It is a visual-regression diff artifact (Diff_ prefix, tests/screenshots/diff/ directory) produced by a CodeceptJS MongoDB 'down nodes' dashboard check, so the image records a panel that failed to render its time series rather than a passing baseline.
nodes.norm_label: mongo down nodes states visual diff screenshot

nodes.label: Node States Grafana Panel
nodes.description: The MongoDB dashboard panel whose title bar reads 'Node States'. In PMM MongoDB dashboards this panel visualizes replica-set member state over time (PRIMARY/SECONDARY/DOWN), which is exactly what a 'down nodes' scenario exercises.

nodes.label: Grafana 'Data does not have a time field' Empty State
nodes.description: Grafana's error/empty rendering shown when a time-series visualization receives a query result frame with no time column. It is the only content in the panel body of this screenshot and is the visual signal a graph-panel assertion would trip on.
nodes.norm_label: grafana 'data does not have a time field' empty state

nodes.label: Visual Regression Diff Artifact Convention
nodes.rationale: CodeceptJS visual-regression (resemble/pixelmatch) helpers write a 'Diff_<name>.png' into tests/screenshots/diff/ only when a captured screenshot fails to match its base image. Committing the diff into the repo preserves the failing pixel evidence so a reviewer can see WHY the comparison failed without re-running the suite; the sibling Diff_test.png in the same directory shows the convention is not one-off.
nodes.description: Naming and directory convention that marks this PNG as failure evidence from an image-comparison assertion rather than a reference baseline.

nodes.label: Diff_test.png (Grafana Panel Time-Series Screenshot)
nodes.rationale: Captured as the rendered-difference output of a visual comparison of a single Grafana time-series panel: a dark-theme chart with a log-scaled y axis (ticks 2, 8, 32, 128), an x axis spanning roughly 16:34:00 to 16:38:30, one flat red/orange series near the top of the scale and one flat yellow series pinned at the bottom. The generic 'test' stem and the fact that no test source in this repo writes to tests/screenshots/diff indicate it is a leftover run artifact committed alongside the suite rather than a referenced fixture.

nodes.label: Visual Regression Diff Artifact
nodes.rationale: Storing the rendered diff image (not just a pass/fail assertion) is what lets a reviewer see which pixels of a dashboard panel moved between the baseline and the run.

nodes.label: Diff_<name>.png Artifact Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: The Diff_ prefix plus the dedicated tests/screenshots/diff folder is the output convention of resemble-style CodeceptJS visual comparison helpers, which keep baseline, actual and diff images in sibling folders so the diff can be identified by filename alone.
